messages:
sara: Heads-up — I repro'd an OOM in prod with the new kernel selector on long-chat flows (redwood-13B-quant, 16xA100). It happens at generation step ~24 when logits scratchpad spikes.

mike: I saw that too. Device mem climbs steadily even though KV cache stays the same size. Looks like scratchpad + activations combined push us over. :face_with_monocle:

dmitri: Pasted a mini profile from the canary run: 
```text
[profile snap]
timestamp: 1769504300
GPU total 40.0GB
used 36.8GB
  activations: 17.9GB
  logits_scratchpad: 13.1GB
  kv_cache: 4.6GB
  freelist_wasted: 0.8GB
peak scratchpad growth at step 24 -> +6.8GB allocation in <150ms
```

katie: Two hypotheses: 1) our scratchpad lifetime isn't being freed promptly when we switch kernels (different codepaths) and 2) freelist fragmentation prevents reuse for the logits buffer so it reallocates large slab.

sara: Repro script below (sanitized). Note the bursty batch shapes (some requests are 1x1024, others 8x256) which mess with continuous batching heuristics.
```bash
# repro harness
run_canary --model redwood-13b-quant --requests-file bursty_shapes.json --kernel-policy selector-v2
```

mike: I tried forcing eager free of logits after each token and it avoids OOMs locally, but it increases CPU overhead and latency for small batches. Tradeoff.

dmitri: Proposed short-term mitigation: enable a compact arena mode that attempts to coalesce small free regions and cap per-stream scratchpad. Config sketch: 
```json
{
  "allocator_mode": "compact_arena",
  "scratchpad_cap": {
    "13B+": "1.5GB",
    "<=6B": "768MB"
  },
  "eager_free_logits": true
}
```

tj: For KV cache interaction we should avoid evicting useful KV pages aggressively, but we can allow transient eviction of largest scratchpad slabs when system-wide mem > 85% and retry allocate after compaction. Basically two-tier fallback: compact, evict_nonhot_kv, fallback-to-cpu-logits.

katie: Ran canary with compact_arena + scratchpad_cap 1.2GB for 13B: no OOMs in 2h stress, peak mem 34.5GB, but p95 latency increased by ~3%. Throughput for large-burst tests dropped ~6% due to more frequent kernel switches.

sara: That's acceptable short-term. Need to avoid regressing SLAs. Action items: (1) ship compact_arena behind flag, (2) add telemetry scratchpad_peak_by_model and freelist_fragmentation_ratio, (3) add graceful fallback to CPU logits for extreme bursts, (4) tune batching heuristics to avoid mixing 1x1024 with 8x256 in same batch where possible.

mike: I'll open the runtime PR for compact_arena + eager_free toggle. Will gate default off.

dmitri: I'll add the telemetry and a canary dashboard. Suggest metric names: `scratchpad.peak_bytes`, `freelist.fragmentation_pct`, `allocator.compactions`

katie: I'll test workload-aware batching rule: when we detect >30% variance in sequence length in the current batching window, split batch into two buckets instead of one. Quick patch reduced scratchpad variance in local runs.

sara: Also let's set KV eviction policy TTL to 30m for interactive sessions and set mem-pressure threshold to 75% to trigger compaction early.

mike: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/402 (compact_arena + opt-in eager_free). Leaving notes on perf tradeoffs. :rocket:

dmitri: Added dashboard PR for telemetry: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/118

infra-bot: deploy-canary job started for runtime/compact_arena (canary cluster: canary-gnode-7)

sara: Great. After canary we should run 24h soak with mixes of bursty shapes and long chats. If stable, roll flag to 10% then 50%.

mike: ACK. I'll also add a small test to the e2e suite that asserts scratchpad_peak < model-specific cap under a synthetic burst.

katie: Observability note: add a per-request header `x-scratchpad-used` we can surface in traces to correlate incoming request shapes to peaks.

sara: Thanks team. Let's sync tomorrow 10am if canary shows anything odd. :eyes:
